Dylan —

Thanks for the details and the spreadsheet — helpful. Initial read (ballpark) and clarifications below.

Ballpark recommendation (reserved capacity, assuming dedicated/private deployment):
- SKU mix: 6x H100 (80GB) + 8x A100 (40GB) as a mixed pool. H100s are prioritized for the RAG-heavy, low-tail workloads; A100s handle steady-state completions and embeddings.
- Estimated serving concurrency capacity: ~95 p95-equivalent concurrent sessions with continuous batching and KV-cache (30% reuse).
- Expected latency (approx): p95 token latency ~120–200ms; p99 tail for streaming tokens in this configuration ~320–420ms depending on sequence-length skew and kernel choices. We can tune kernels for the lower end but reserve buffer for spikes.
- Autoscale & burst: Recommend a small on-demand burst fleet (hot-standby) to cover the 2.5x promo spikes; prefer burst to be a mix of additional A100s and temporary H100 rentals rather than permanent commit.
- Cost control: aggressive batching for simple completions and a routing rule to fallback to smaller model family during extreme bursts (with transparent quality flags).

Clarifying questions for NascentAI (to confirm before final proposal):
1) Of the RAG flows, what % require synchronous vector lookups within the same LLM call vs asynchronous retrieval? Synchronous lookups increase p99 pressure.
2) For streaming, are you streaming at token granularity (every token) or chunked (50–100 token chunks)? Token-level streaming is costlier on tail latency.
3) What fraction of calls include external retrieval that could be cached at the application layer?

I’ll draft a simple fleet plan (PDF) with exact GPU counts and estimated monthly committed units for procurement. Attaching draft: nascentai_draft_fleet_plan.pdf.

-Marissa Cole
Principal Product Manager, Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference
